body:
Claude: **must-fix**: The percentage offsets and the jitter are derived from `service->rr->ttl` (the raw, unclamped network TTL) but anchored at `service->until`, which the cache clamps to `CACHE_TTL_MAX_USEC` (2 h) past the caching timestamp. The two quantities are not commensurate, and the result is an event armed *after* the cache entry has already expired.

Once `(100 - percent) * ttl / 100` exceeds the available window `until - usec`, the loop skips 80/85/90/95% and settles on `DNS_RECORD_TTL_STATE_100_PERCENT`, where the offset is zero and `next_time == until` exactly. Line 116 then adds up to 2% of the raw TTL on top, so the source fires strictly after the record expired. `mdns_maintenance_query()` treats the 100% state as "do not query, just revisit the cache" (line 151), and the revisit prunes the now-expired entry, so the service is dropped without a single refresh query ever being sent — the same "never requeried, drops off the browse list" symptom the commit message sets out to fix, reached through the cache cap instead of the 32-bit wrap.

This is not only an exotic-TTL case. It triggers whenever 5% of the TTL exceeds the remaining window: for advertised TTLs above ~144000 s (where `until - usec` is pinned at 2 h), and more routinely for any `dns_add_new_service()` on a record already in the last 5% of its cached lifetime — e.g. a browser subscribing 4400 s into a 4500 s PTR record, where 5% = 225 s > 100 s remaining, so the state jumps to 100% and up to 90 s of jitter arms the event past expiry.

The `next_time = usec_add(usec, USEC_PER_SEC)` fallback at line 112 is likewise meant to fire promptly, but line 116 adds the same jitter to it, so "in one second" becomes up to 2% of an arbitrary 32-bit TTL later.

Deriving the increments and the jitter from the effective remaining lifetime (`service->until - usec`) rather than the raw TTL would make the quantities commensurate; at minimum, clamp the jitter to the window actually left (`MIN(jitter, until - next_time)`) and skip it entirely on the fallback branch.
